A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OPTIMAS work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G support comparison, including matching content moved between the appendices and main text.

before.justification: v3 reports original experiments on five compound-system tasks, with performance comparisons, alignment and interpretability studies, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds single-LLM and REINFORCE comparisons in Table 2 and cost and timing results in Appendix G.4.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 and Algorithm 1 change adaptation from updating the selected component’s LRF before local optimization to updating all LRFs after an accepted configuration change, retaining them after rejection. This revises the adaptation procedure within the same backbone, ranking objective, and local optimizers. Figure 3 still describes the earlier ordering.

E1.justification: Both versions use Amazon recommendation, PubMedQA classification, STaRK-Prime retrieval, HotpotQA, and BigCodeBench. The added comparators and cost analysis introduce no additional datasets, task requirements, or evaluation environments.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds a direct single-LLM reference across all five tasks and REINFORCE on Amazon, substantially expanding the controls for compound-system design and optimization with global rewards. Previous comparators remain. Table 4 shortens the LLM Judge label, but its stated 20-example setting is retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D and Table 5 revise Amazon’s two local models from Qwen 2.5 1B to 1.5B; this establishes a reported setting change, not that experiments were rerun. The new REINFORCE experiment specifies 16 rollouts per step, learning rate 1e-5, and 100 training steps. Existing dataset splits and task metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix G.4 analyzes Amazon’s initialization, adaptation, validation, and PPO costs. Existing alignment, interpretability, and sensitivity analyses remain. The training-data and backbone-size studies now combined in main-text Figure 7 already appeared in v3’s appendix.

E5.justification: Appendix G.4 newly states that local-optimization timing is averaged over five runs. This adds run-count reporting without establishing additional benchmark repetitions or seeds. Existing performance uncertainty reporting is retained; the new Table 2 rows use the same plus/minus presentation.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds five single-LLM results and Amazon REINFORCE accuracy of 21.89±2.65, making REINFORCE the strongest reported Amazon baseline. Previously reported scores, including OPTIMAS’s 24.24±0.82 there, remain unchanged. Appendix G.4 adds cost components and timing estimates; existing cost totals and relocated sensitivity results are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.1 changes the maximizer of the negative ranking loss to its minimizer, and Lemma B.1 changes log-likelihood minimization to maximization. These correct mathematical optimization directions. The remaining assumptions and proofs are largely retained, and formal Theorem B.1 still contains the earlier maximizer wording.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: heterogeneous component optimization through adaptive globally aligned local rewards, convergence under stated conditions, and data efficiency. The headline five-task improvement claim remains 11.92%.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 explicitly discusses the absence of general global-optimality guarantees for nonconvex problems and adds mention of Kurdyka–Łojasiewicz conditions. Appendix G.4 interprets efficiency using equal component costs and trajectory caching, while identifying additional PPO overhead for trainable components. Interpretations accompanying the relocated sensitivity studies are retained.

D1.justification: v4 adds REINFORCE hyperparameters, Amazon preference and validation budgets, caching details, and PPO hardware and timing information. Section 4.1 clarifies that non-downstream outputs remain fixed during reward estimation. Conversely, it removes the direct anonymous-repository link and the three-epoch specification for the training-data-size study; the project website remains listed.

R1.justification: v4 adds Williams (1992), citing it in related work and for the new REINFORCE baseline. The remaining cited works and positioning around heterogeneous optimization and adaptive reward modeling are substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 makes localized grammar and algorithm-description edits, brings existing efficiency discussion into Section 5.2, and reorganizes Appendix G accordingly. It also updates conference headers and contribution footnotes, adds acknowledgements, and gives ethics and reproducibility statements separate headings. The overall narrative structure remains recognizable.

P2.justification: v4 combines v3’s appendix Figure 7 and backbone-size Table 9 into main-text Figure 7, with revised labeling and caption. Table 2 gains comparator rows, and new Table 11 displays the cost breakdown. Other appendix tables are renumbered, while Figures 1–6 retain their displays.

improvement.justification: The added comparators, cost breakdown, and partial mathematical corrections offer benefits. However, moving adaptation in Algorithm 1 leaves next-iteration reward parameters referenced before definition, and G.4 does not reconcile five 12-minute single-GPU runs with six GPU-hours. Table 2 also retains a 14.3% Amazon improvement despite the new baseline implying about 10.7%. These issues affect reproducibility and the central performance and efficiency evidence, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
